Then, applying Cloude and Freeman decomposition on it to achieve scattering entropy H, average scattering angle α and three scattering mechanisms, involving canopy scatter, first-order Bragg surface scatter, and a double-bounce scattering mechanism. We apply these methods to fully polarimetric radar data from a classical dihedral in ground clutter and get the ideal results, i.e. the target is recognized in both algorithms. Therefore, there is no doubt that target decomposition(TD) theorems offer great potential in detecting and recognizing targets under the ground clutter.

articleTitle: GPU+COW parallel computing system to accelerate the FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: Since Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method was proposed by Yee in 1966, its hardware acceleration problem arouses much concern. In this paper, how to use GPU+COW parallel computing system to accelerate the FDTD method was introduced briefly. The acceleration scheme and the simulation results were presented, and then the feasibility and efficiency of the proposed scheme were proved.

articleTitle: Design of a Ka-band Microstrip quasi-Yagi antenna array based on LTCC substrate
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: A Microstrip-fed quasi-Yagi phased array antenna at Ka-band is designed. This linear antenna array is constituted by 8 microstrip patch unit based on low-temperature co-fired-ceramic (LTCC) substrate(FerroA6M), it has several advantages, e.g., strong direction, broad bandwidth, easy-integration with LTCC circuit systems. 3D EM simulator was utilized to analyse the simulation of the antenna array. Simulation results indicate that the proposed antenna has 16dB gain at 35GHz and 2G bandwidth with less than −14 dB return loss, meanwhile, achieves the scan range of ± 25° without grating lobes. The bandwidth of the array antenna are 22.9% when VSWR<2, respectively. There is a very broad application prospect in LTCC-technology wireless communication system on the antenna.

articleTitle: TDIE-MOT solvers based on PMCHWT and Muller equations for transient scattering by 2D dielectric objects
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: An accurate numerical procedure for analyses of transient scattering by two-dimensional dielectric objects by using the Time Domain Integral Equation (TDIE) method based on PMCHWT equations and Muller equations is developed. The Marching On-in Time (MOT) scheme is employed to solve the integral equations. Quadratic B-spline function is used as the temporal basis functions, and closed-form integrals with respect to time are derived to calculate the matrix elements precisely. Numerical results demonstrate that both the PMCHWT and Muller approaches are accurate and stable for a range of relative permittivity in comparisons with the frequency domain results via discrete Fourier transforms. The Muller approach may be preferred to the PMCHWT scheme for small relative permittivity; however, the PMCHWT approach seems more dependable in general cases.

articleTitle: Design of high-speed data playback board based on AD9739
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: This paper gives a brief introduction of a high-speed playback board which has multi-channel synchronization function. FPGA is controller and AD9739 is playback chip. By choosing hardware and configuring software, the board can be used as single-channel, dual-channel, three-channel and four-channel data playback board. When the operating mode is selected as a channel with four paths, playback rate can be up to 10Gsps. Synchronization error between channels can be as small as 40ps. This paper focuses on the hardware and software implementation of target DA board.

articleTitle: Investigation of ultra-wideband pulses radiation by aperture stacked patch antennas and linear arrays
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: A low-profile ultra-wideband aperture stacked patch antenna is investigated as a radiator of ultra-wideband radio pulses with 50% relative bandwidth. Antenna design is based on low permittivity materials such as Rogers RO 4003, teflon and foam. On the basis of proposed stacked patch a 4-element linear antenna array was designed and investigated. Frequency-domain results demonstrated very good array elements matching and negligible mutual coupling. Simulated radiated transient pulses are presented for different observation angles, energy patterns and fidelity factors are calculated. Time-domain results evidence small radiated pulse degradation and high fidelity factor values for broadside directions.

articleTitle: Design of X band low phase noise dielectric resonator oscillator
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: Microwave dielectric oscillation frequency source uses a small size, light weight, high Q value, inexpensive dielectric resonator (DR) as a resonant unit. It has the advantages of miniaturization, low phase noise, high stability and low cost and had already been widely applied, so the research on microwave dielectric oscillator has also become one of the focus of today's microwave integrated circuits. [1] This paper describes the working principle and design method of the DRO. Through reading lots of literature on DROs, the author has deeply knows about the theory of DROs and designs a circuit with both HFSS and ADS simulation software.

articleTitle: Realization of linear polarization reconfiguration for mobile satcom in Ku-band
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: In this paper, we have outlined a realization of linear polarization reconfiguration for mobile satellite communication in Ku-band. Waveguide antenna is selected for the polarization reconfiguration, which is capable of realizing double transmission channels for frequency-reuse transceivers. And the polarization reconfiguration subsystem can also weaken the cross-polarized interference. The experimental results show that the design is effective and feasible.

articleTitle: Analysis of bistatic location of optimal station distribution under different geometric distribution
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: In this paper, based on the analysis of the principle of double cross positioning, the selected target placed on the positioning baseline's perpendicular bisector so as to cross-positioning and the positioning model under different geometric distribution conditions is established which is on the positioning baseline's perpendicular bisector, the target distance, lateral angle which are the key factors affecting the accuracy of positioning are analyzed, the best station configuration of bistatic location under the conditions of different geometric distribution was obtained.

articleTitle: W-band monopulse radar antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: In this paper, the method for formatting sequential rotation subarray and the far field function are studied. Simulate a formatting sequential rotation subarray with four microstip antenna subarrays at 93GHz. The impendance bandwith determined from a 1.5 VSWR is 3.3GHz. The gain was approximately 24dB, and null depth is over 40dB.

articleTitle: Taguchi method for analysing the C shape DGS' frequency characteristic
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: The frequency characteristics of the microstrip line with DGS are simulated by means of 3-D field analysis, and its equivalent circuit and equivalent parameters extraction are analyzed. Then the influences of C shape and the material permittivity on frequency characteristic are discussed using the simulation with Taguchi method.

articleTitle: Radio simulation training platform design based on components
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: The cost performance of radio simulation software is not high because of radio's characteristics of variety frequent update and complete function. An idea of radio simulation training platform design based on components is put forward through analyzing of the various components and functions of the radio. The article design functions and technical architectures of the simulation platform. Component implementation methods are discussed. The platform is primarily developed in work. That proves the idea's feasibility.

articleTitle: A high gain wideband Minkowski T-probe coupled patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: Thispaperpresents thedesign of high gain wide-band Minkowski single -layer T-probe coupled patch antenna, using a T-probe to feed a single layer patch antenna along withfractal geometry, the antenna bandwidth, gain are remarkable increased, antenna size is reduced about 70%of its original size and more importantly radiation pattern is stable across entire pass-band. The simulated gain is above 11dBi, upper and lower frequency ratio is 3.3. The antenna bandwidth covers IEEE.11a 5.8GHz, ISM2.45GHz, WIMAX (3.2–3.8GHz)satellite TV in Ku band (11.7–12.2GHz) and other useful frequencyband. To explore antenna performance such as return loss, gain, radiation pattern CST Microwave Studio 2012 is used and measured S11 is presented.

articleTitle: A 8-output compact broadband Wilkinson power divider in LTCC technology
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: Recently, there has been significant interest in passive devices fabricated using LTCC technology, for which makes the 3D structure of the transmission lines realizable. In this paper, a compact broadband 8-output Wilkinson power divider at 0.5∼1.5GHz in LTCC technology is presented. The power divider is designed in two-section to achieve the broadband, and some λ/4impedance transformations are used to broaden the line width, for reaching the technical requirements in LTCC. The simulation results show a phase error of less than +/− 3° and a power imbalance at output port of less than 0.4dB from 0.5∼1.5GHz. The insertion loss is better than 2.8dB and isolation is better than 15dB. The whole size of the multilayer integrated device is 25mm×25mm×2.1mm.

articleTitle: Metamaterials applied in half-wave dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: In recent years, Metamaterials is widely applied in the field of microwave, include in the field of antenna studies, but little of them come down to half wave antenna and antenna array. So a half wave dipole antenna and antenna array are simulated as a benchmark, antennas loading reflector, metal reflective plate and Metamaterials reflective plate are simulated respectively. The simulation results show that the Metamaterials can effectively increase the antenna's and array's gain, especially the side-fire antenna array's gain.

articleTitle: Novel design of 4 elements GPS antenna array with UC-EBG structure
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: In this paper, a novel 4 elements GPS antenna array with UC-EBG structure is proposed for GPS navigation application. In order to achieve higher gain and lower backward radiation, the UC-EBG structure is added into the 4 elements antenna array. The effects of the UC-EBG structure on reflection coefficient and radiation performance are investigated. It is found that the gain and backward radiation can be better by choosing proper design parameters of the UC-EBG.

articleTitle: High gain L twin probe fed patch antenna for dual-band WLAN2.4/5GHz &WIMAX applications
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: A dual band antenna design is proposed and studied in this paper. The actual dual band operation is achieved by using the in phase L twin in form of V shape. The simulation study reveal that antenna can cover the useful two WLAN bands namely IEEE standards 802.11a b/g(2.4–2.4835GHz and 5WLAN), WIMAX bands (2.5–2.8GHz, 3.2–3.8GHz), and satellite TV in C band (3.7–4.2GHz). With proper dimensions choice antenna has been succefully radiate in two bands low band 2.2–3GHz and high band 3.3–6.25GHz with maximum gain 5.6dBi and 10.3dBi respectively, parameters dimensions can also be adjusted to achieve an ultra-wide band operation (2.2–6.5GHz) details of the design process are described in the sections to follow CST MWS 2012 is used as simulator tool.

articleTitle: Design of 8mm Ka-band broadband LNA
publicationTitle: 2013 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROWAVE TECHNOLOGY & COMPUTATIONAL ELECTROMAGNETICS
abstract: The HEMT model in this article is applied by OMMIC D01PH. In this article we design a five circuit, the first two levels are designed for minimum noise and the last three for maximum gain design. The center frequency of this design is 35 GHz with 6 GHz bandwidth, gain is greater than 30dB and the noise figure is less than 3dB. This article describes a Ka-band low-noise amplifier design idea. In this idea we put up two options for the bias circuit design, one is drain supply by a single power and the other is dual-power supply for the drain and gate. We make circuit design and simulation for each program and the simulation results were analyzed and compared.
